A desktop developer workbench that stitches together terminals, a file viewer, Git, and
remote (SSH) workspaces into a single Electron application.

hvir is designed for people who spend their day switching between a terminal, a file
tree, a diff, and a Git graph. It runs the same UI against local folders and remote SSH
hosts, so working "on the other machine" feels the same as working locally.

## Features

- **Fast, native terminals** — powered by [`node-pty`](https://github.com/microsoft/node-pty)
  in the main process and a customized [ghostty-web](https://github.com/jarmak-personal/ghostty-web)
  renderer, with theming, splits, and multi-workspace attention badges.
- **Code viewer** — a [CodeMirror 6](https://codemirror.net/) viewer with tabs, split
  panes, diff view, [Shiki](https://shiki.style/) syntax highlighting, Markdown preview
  (`markdown-it` + task lists), and [Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org/) diagrams.
- **Git-native workflow** — status, staging, diff, branch switching, worktrees, fetch,
  pull, and a Git graph view coordinated through a dedicated worker.
- **Remote workspaces over SSH** — open a project on a remote host with the same file
  tree, viewer, and terminals; SSH prompts are handled by the app.
- **Document review mode** — a workspace mode purpose-built for reading a set of
  changes side-by-side with the terminal.
- **HTML preview** — a sandboxed `hvir-preview:` protocol for previewing rendered
  Markdown, Mermaid, and other HTML content.
- **Workspaces & sessions** — projects, session dialogs, and per-workspace layout are
  persisted so a restart puts everything back where it was.

## Platforms

hvir targets desktop platforms with signed installers:

- **macOS** — Apple Silicon (`arm64`) `.pkg` installers, hardened runtime, installed
  under `/Applications`.
- **Linux** — Debian packages (`.deb`) for `x64` and `arm64`, with an AppArmor profile
  and post-install hooks.

Windows is not a supported packaging target today.

## Requirements

- **Node.js** — `>= 24` (enforced by `engines` in `package.json`).
- **npm** — bundled with your Node.js install.
- **Native toolchain** — required for `node-gyp` to build the private
  `@hvir/rename-noreplace` Node-API addon and to rebuild `node-pty` against the
  Electron ABI.
  - macOS: Xcode Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`).
  - Linux: `build-essential`, `python3`, and standard headers.
- **Electron** — installed automatically by the `postinstall` hook.

## Getting started

Clone the repository and install dependencies. The `postinstall` script fetches the
Electron runtime, rebuilds the native addons, and prepares `node-pty` for Electron's
Node ABI:

```bash
npm install
```

Run the app in development against the current source tree:

```bash
npm run dev
```

`electron-vite` will start the main, preload, and renderer bundles and open a hvir
window.

## Building

Produce a production build (typecheck, then bundle main + preload + renderer):

```bash
npm run build
```

Package installers with `electron-builder`:

```bash
# macOS (Apple Silicon .pkg)
npm run pack:mac:arm64

# Signed macOS build (requires code-signing environment)
npm run pack:mac:arm64:signed

# Linux .deb
npm run pack:linux:x64
npm run pack:linux:arm64
```

Signed macOS builds require the usual Apple Developer signing environment
(`CSC_LINK`, `CSC_KEY_PASSWORD`, notarization credentials, etc.) — see
`electron-builder.yml` for the exact entitlements and installer configuration.

hvir ships with a full verification pipeline. The `verify` script runs the same checks
CI runs and is the recommended pre-push command:

```bash
npm run verify
```

Individual checks are also exposed:

```bash
npm run lint              # ESLint
npm run typecheck         # tsc for node + web projects
npm test                  # Vitest
npm run test:watch        # Vitest in watch mode
npm run test:mutation     # Stryker mutation tests
npm run check-seams       # Architectural seam enforcement
npm run check-adrs        # ADR consistency check
npm run architecture:check # Architecture hotspot budget
npm run format            # Prettier (write)
npm run format:check      # Prettier (check only)
```

### Smoke and acceptance tests

The end-to-end scenarios drive a real Electron build against synthetic workspaces:

```bash
npm run smoke              # Full scenario suite
npm run smoke:macos        # macOS-focused subset
npm run smoke:linux:installed  # From an installed .deb package
npm run smoke:macos:installed  # From an installed .pkg
npm run smoke:isolation    # Interruption/isolation coverage
```

Real-host SSH acceptance runs against a live SSH server:

```bash
npm run acceptance:ssh:macos
npm run acceptance:ssh:real-host
```

```
src/
  main/       Electron main process — window, IPC, PTY, Git, SSH, workspaces
  preload/    Preload scripts bridging main and renderer
  renderer/   React 19 UI — terminal, viewer, Git panel, workspaces, settings
  shared/     Types and IPC contracts shared across processes
  workers/    Worker entry points (echo, Git worker host, etc.)
packages/
  rename-noreplace/  Private Node-API addon for atomic cross-directory rename
scripts/    Build, release, smoke, and project-management scripts
build/      Icons, entitlements, Linux packaging helpers, native binaries
test/       Test helpers and fixtures
```

## Git hooks

Install the repository's Git hooks (formatting and lint gates) into your local clone:

```bash
npm run hooks:install
```
